title: Dimension at a point of a finite type affine scheme from its irreducible components
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in X$ correspond to a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset S$. Then the Krull dimension of $X$ at $x$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals the maximum of the Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (with the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]) of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ which contain $x$. Equivalently, if $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ are the minimal prime ideals of $S$ (prime ideals containing no strictly smaller prime ideal) contained in $\mathfrak p$, then $t\ge1$ and $$\dim_xX=\max_{1\le i\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i),$$ where the right hand side uses ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; this is a non-negative integer. It also equals the minimum of $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ over the maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and this minimum is attained.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OT (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27787-27848), especially equality of (1) and (2); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00OT,algebra-lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field)

proof.text: Setup. Write $V(I)=\{\mathfrak P\in X: I\subseteq\mathfrak P\}$ for an ideal $I\subseteq S$; these are the closed subsets of $X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $x=\mathfrak p$. The field $k$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $S$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and has only finitely many minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. The irreducible components of $X$ are exactly the sets $V(\mathfrak q_1),\dots,V(\mathfrak q_r)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], and they are pairwise distinct since $V(\mathfrak q_j)\subseteq V(\mathfrak q_l)$ iff $\mathfrak q_l\subseteq\mathfrak q_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (1). By the same part (1), $x=\mathfrak p\in V(\mathfrak q_j)$ iff $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Put $I'=\{j:\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$: the irreducible components through $x$ are the $V(\mathfrak q_j)$, $j\in I'$, and the minimal primes contained in $\mathfrak p$ (the $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ of the statement) are the $\mathfrak q_j$, $j\in I'$. $I'\neq\emptyset$, since $\mathfrak p$ contains a minimal prime of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] (with $I=0$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'Let X = union of the Z_i be the decomposition of X into its irreducible components. There are finitely many of them (see Lemmas 00FN lemma-obvious-Noetherian and 00FR lemma-Noetherian-topology). Let I' = {i | x in Z_i}'; 'Let q_i denote the minimal primes of S corresponding to the irreducible components Z_i' (Lemma 00ES (3))

proof.text: The dimensions of the components. Fix $j$ and let $\pi_j:S\to S/\mathfrak q_j$ be the quotient map. $S/\mathfrak q_j$ is an integral domain ($\mathfrak q_j$ is prime) and a finite type $k$-algebra (compose a surjection $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ with $\pi_j$) [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; it is nonzero, so it has a maximal ideal [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] says that $d_j:=\dim(S/\mathfrak q_j)$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is a non-negative integer. The map $\operatorname{Spec}(S/\mathfrak q_j)\to X$, $\bar{\mathfrak P}\mapsto\pi_j^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak P})$, is a homeomorphism onto $V(\mathfrak q_j)$ with its subspace topology [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], so the Krull dimension of the space $V(\mathfrak q_j)$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals that of the space $\operatorname{Spec}(S/\mathfrak q_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension], which is $d_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $N=\max_{j\in I'}d_j$, the maximum of a finite nonempty set of non-negative integers (step 1). By step 1, $N$ is both the maximum of the dimensions of the irreducible components of $X$ through $x$ and $\max_{1\le i\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i)$ over the minimal primes $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak p$; so the two forms of the statement agree, and it remains to show $\dim_xX=N$ and $\min_{\mathfrak m}\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})=N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'The number (2) is max_{i in I'} dim(Z_i)'; Z_i = V(q_i) is homeomorphic to Spec(S/q_i) (Lemma 00E5 lemma-spec-closed), and dim of a ring is dim of its spectrum (Definition 00KE)

proof.text: Chains through a minimal prime. Let $j\in\{1,\dots,r\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] the map $\bar{\mathfrak P}\mapsto\pi_j^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak P})$ is a bijection from the primes of $S/\mathfrak q_j$ onto the primes of $S$ containing $\mathfrak q_j$, with inverse $\mathfrak P\mapsto\pi_j(\mathfrak P)$; both maps preserve inclusion (preimage and image of sets do), hence strict inclusion. (a) If $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_s$ are primes of $S$, then $\pi_j(\mathfrak P_0)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\pi_j(\mathfrak P_s)$ is a chain of primes of $S/\mathfrak q_j$, so $s\le d_j$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. (b) If $\mathfrak m$ is a maximal ideal of $S$ with $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak m$, then $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})\ge d_j$. Indeed $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\pi_j(\mathfrak m)$ is a maximal ideal of $S/\mathfrak q_j$ (as $(S/\mathfrak q_j)/\bar{\mathfrak m}\cong S/\mathfrak m$ is a field), so $d_j=\dim((S/\mathfrak q_j)_{\bar{\mathfrak m}})$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] (step 2), which is the supremum of the lengths $s$ of chains $\bar{\mathfrak P}_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\bar{\mathfrak P}_s\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak m}$ of primes of $S/\mathfrak q_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. Each such chain gives the chain $\pi_j^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak P}_0)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\pi_j^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak P}_s)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ of primes of $S$, so $s\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] for $S$ and $\mathfrak m$. Hence $d_j\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'For each i such that x_0 in Z_i (which is equivalent to m containing q_i) we have a surjection S_m -> S_m/q_i S_m = (S/q_i)_m ... We conclude, using Lemma 00OS (lemma-dimension-spell-it-out), that the dimension of S_m is the maximum of the dimensions of the Z_i passing through x_0'; the source gets the upper bound from Lemma 00ET (the q_i S_m exhaust the minimal primes of S_m), here replaced by the chain count (a) and step 9

proof.text: Lower bound for the local rings. Let $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ be a maximal ideal of $S$. For $j\in I'$ we have $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})\ge d_j$ by step 3 (b). Taking the maximum over $j\in I'$: $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})\ge N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'First of all, x_0 is contained in all the irreducible components Z_i, i in I''

proof.text:
Maximal ideals in a neighbourhood. Let $W\subseteq X$ be open with $\mathfrak p\in W$. The sets $D(f)=\{\mathfrak P: f
otin\mathfrak P\}$ form a basis of the topology [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (i), so there is $f\in S$ with $\mathfrak p\in D(f)\subseteq W$, i.e. $f
otin\mathfrak p$. Since $S$ is a finite type $k$-algebra, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal] gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ with $f
otin\mathfrak m$, i.e. $\mathfrak m\in D(f)\subseteq W$. So every open neighbourhood of $x$ contains a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'Note that each W_i, i in I' contains a closed point because X is Jacobson, see Section 00FZ (section-ring-jacobson)' and 'Because S is Jacobson (as we saw above) it is enough to show that V(p) minus T is nonempty'; the Jacobson property is Lemma 00G1 (lemma-finite-type-field-Jacobson)

proof.text: Lower bound for the neighbourhoods: $\dim W\ge N$ for every open $W\ni x$, where $\dim W$ is the Krull dimension of $W$ with the subspace topology [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Take $\mathfrak m\in W$ as in step 5 and a chain $\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_s\subseteq\mathfrak m$ of primes of $S$. The sets $V(\mathfrak P_l)$ are irreducible closed subsets of $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (2), they contain $\mathfrak m\in W$ (part (1), as $\mathfrak P_l\subseteq\mathfrak m$), so they meet $W$, and $V(\mathfrak P_s)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V(\mathfrak P_0)$ (part (1): $V(\mathfrak P)\subseteq V(\mathfrak P')$ iff $\mathfrak P'\subseteq\mathfrak P$). By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] the sets $V(\mathfrak P_l)\cap W$ are irreducible closed subsets of $W$ and $V(\mathfrak P_s)\cap W\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V(\mathfrak P_0)\cap W$, a chain of length $s$; so $\dim W\ge s$. Taking the supremum over such chains, $\dim W\ge\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], and $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})\ge N$ by step 4.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'The existence of a closed point implies, via Lemma 00OS (lemma-dimension-spell-it-out), that there is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length equal to dim(Z_i) in the open W_i'; here one closed point m in W containing p serves all i in I' at once

proof.text:
The neighbourhood $U$ and the upper bound $\dim U\le N$. Let $T= igcup_{j
otin I'}V(\mathfrak q_j)$, a finite union of closed sets, hence closed, and $U=X\setminus T$, open; $\mathfrak p
otin V(\mathfrak q_j)$ for $j
otin I'$ (step 1), so $x\in U$. Let $Y_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Y_s$ be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $U$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] their closures $\overline{Y_l}$ in $X$ are irreducible closed subsets of $X$ meeting $U$, with $\overline{Y_0}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\overline{Y_s}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (2),(1) $\overline{Y_l}=V(\mathfrak P_l)$ for primes with $\mathfrak P_s\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_0$. $\mathfrak P_s$ contains a minimal prime of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], one of the $\mathfrak q_j$ (step 1). Then $V(\mathfrak P_s)\subseteq V(\mathfrak q_j)$ and $V(\mathfrak P_s)$ meets $U$, so $V(\mathfrak q_j)
ot\subseteq T$, i.e. $j\in I'$. The chain $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak P_s\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_0$ gives $s\le d_j\le N$ by step 3 (a). Hence $\dim U\le N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'let T = union of the Z_i, i not in I'. Then U = X minus T is an open subset of X containing the point x ... For any open W in U with x in W the irreducible components of W are the irreducible sets W_i = Z_i cap W for i in I' ... Since W_i in Z_i we have dim(W_i) <= dim(Z_i)'

proof.text: (1) = (2). By definition [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] $\dim_xX$ is the minimum of $\dim W$ over the open $W\ni x$. By step 6 every such $W$ has $\dim W\ge N$, and the open $U\ni x$ of step 7 has $\dim U\le N$. Hence $\dim_xX=\dim U=N$, which by step 2 is the maximum of the dimensions of the irreducible components through $x$ and equals $\max_{1\le i\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852): 'Hence dim(W) is equal to the number (2). This proves that (1) = (2).'

proof.text: (2) = (3). By step 5 applied to $W=U$ there is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0\supseteq\mathfrak p$ with $\mathfrak m_0\in U$. Let $\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_s\subseteq\mathfrak m_0$ be a chain of primes of $S$. $\mathfrak P_0$ contains a minimal prime $\mathfrak q_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] (step 1); then $\mathfrak q_j\subseteq\mathfrak m_0$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_0\in V(\mathfrak q_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (1), and $\mathfrak m_0\notin T$, so $j\in I'$; step 3 (a) gives $s\le d_j\le N$. Taking the supremum, $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m_0})\le N$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. With step 4, $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m_0})=N\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ for every maximal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$; so the minimum of $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ over the maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ exists, is attained at $\mathfrak m_0$ and equals $N=\dim_xX$ (step 8).

lean.statement: theorem dimension_at_point_components {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] : let X := Spec (CommRingCat.of S) let x : X := ⟨p, inferInstance⟩ ∃ qs : Finset (Ideal S), (∀ q : Ideal S, q ∈ qs ↔ q.IsPrime ∧ q ≤ p ∧ ∀ r : Ideal S, r.IsPrime → r ≤ q → r = q) ∧ qs.Nonempty ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt x = n ∧ (∀ Z : Set X, Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X → x ∈ Z → topologicalKrullDim Z ≤ n) ∧ (∃ Z : Set X, Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X ∧ x ∈ Z ∧ topologicalKrullDim Z = n) ∧ (∀ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) ≤ n) ∧ (∃ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) = n) ∧ (∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal], p ≤ m → (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m)) ∧ (∃ (m : Ideal S) (_ : m.IsMaximal), p ≤ m ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m) = n)
